info.name: Credential-service
info.description:
Manual test collection for the credential-service Go API.

Set the `base_url` variable if the service isn't running on the default localhost:8080.

Credential types: PAN, GST, FSSAI, UDYAM all resolve on both `/verify-identity` and `/credential` — they share one `VerifierRegistry`, and `/verify-identity` has no per-type restriction, so anything registered there is reachable from either endpoint. `PAN_TO_GST` is the one credential type from the original design doc that was never implemented (no registry entry, no enum row) — it's the collection's example of a genuinely unsupported cred_type.

request.description: Synchronous verification, proxies straight to Digio and returns Digio's response body verbatim — including when Digio itself rejects the credential (still HTTP 200 from this API; inspect the body for Digio's own rejection code/message, e.g. this sample PAN is only valid in shape and Digio's sandbox will reject it with `{"code":"BAD_REQUEST","message":"Invalid Pan Number Detected"}`). Only a real transport failure (Digio unreachable) returns a 502 from this API. name/dob are required for PAN (sent through to Digio) and are ignored for GST.

cred_id must be 14 digits. Hits Digio's `/client/v4/apis/kyc/fetch_id_data/FSSAI` endpoint — a different base path than PAN/GST's v3 endpoint. This sample id is only valid in shape (borrowed from a real Digio response example, not a live license) — expect Digio to reject it (still HTTP 200 from this API; the response body is Digio's own error verbatim). name/dob are not applicable to FSSAI and are ignored if sent. Not originally documented under "Identity Verification API" in the design doc (that section only ever named PAN/GST) — reachable here only because it shares the same VerifierRegistry `/credential` uses; see CLAUDE.md.

cred_id accepts either the canonical hyphenated form shown here (UDYAM-XX-00-0000000) or the compact form with no separators (e.g. UDYAMMH011234567) — both are normalized to the hyphenated form before being sent to Digio. Hits `/client/v4/apis/kyc/fetch_id_data/UDYAMAADHAAR`. This sample id is only valid in shape, not a live registration — expect a Digio-side rejection (still HTTP 200 here). Digio is documented to flap on this endpoint (the same valid Udyam number sometimes 200s with no data); the async `/credential` path retries automatically on that, but this synchronous endpoint does not — a flaky empty response reaches you directly as a failure with no automatic second attempt.
Expect 400 {"error":"name is required"}. name/dob are required_if cred_type=PAN; the same request with cred_type=GST (or FSSAI/UDYAM) would succeed without them.

Expect 400 {"error":"unsupported credential type: PAN_TO_GST"}. PAN_TO_GST is named in the original design doc but was never implemented (no VerifierRegistry entry, no enum row) — it's the one genuinely unsupported cred_type left. (UDYAM used to be this example before it was implemented in Phase 8 — it now resolves successfully, see "Verify UDYAM" above.)

Flat request shape per the design doc's Credential API (cred_type, cred_id, name, dob at the top level — no nested cred_data). name/dob are required for PAN and ignored for other types. participant_id/domain from the doc are intentionally not yet supported (Phase 2 of docs/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md). Paste the response's request_id into the {{request_id}} collection variable to use with "Get Credential Results" below.

cred_id must be 14 digits. Added in Phase 8 (docs/IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md) — endpoint/response shapes sourced from team_pipeline_2807.py's verify_fssai(), not the design doc (which never documented FSSAI's real Digio contract). Digio returns one of two response shapes for FSSAI; both are handled. This sample id is shape-valid only, not a live license — check GET /credential afterwards to see the worker's actual result (likely FAILED against the real Digio sandbox).

cred_id accepts either the canonical hyphenated form shown here or the compact form (e.g. UDYAMMH011234567) — normalized before reaching Digio. Added in Phase 8; endpoint/response shape sourced from team_pipeline_2807.py's verify_udyam(), not the design doc. Digio is documented to flap on this endpoint (a valid Udyam number sometimes 200s with no data) — this async path is the reason that flakiness is tolerable at all: a 200-with-no-UAN response is treated as a soft failure and retried automatically (up to max_retries), unlike the synchronous /verify-identity endpoint. This sample id is shape-valid only, not a live registration.

item.name: Submit Credentials - Multiple in one batch (all 4 types)

request.description: Each credential in the batch is processed independently — one item's failure or retry doesn't affect the others. Response echoes cred_id per item (added in Round 4) so same-type duplicates in a batch stay distinguishable. Paste the request_id into {{request_id}} and use "Get Credential Results" to see all four outcomes.
Missing cred_type should fail dto validation before ever reaching the DB.

Expect 400 — PAN_TO_GST has no VerifierRegistry entry or enum row (named in the original design doc, never implemented; see Implementation Status in Credential Service Implementation Plan.md). Rejected during SubmitCredentials' pre-persistence validation, before anything is written to credential_requests.
Expect 400 {"error":"name is required"} — name/dob are required_if cred_type=PAN, validated before ever reaching the service/DB.

Fetch the results of a previously submitted /credential request (paste the request_id from a Submit Credentials response into the {{request_id}} variable, or replace it inline). request_id is a query param, not a path segment — a bare path segment there would be ambiguous between the batch's request_id and one credential's own id. The response's `credentials` array echoes each submitted `cred_id` alongside our internal `id`, so multiple same-type credentials in one batch (e.g. two PANs) can still be told apart. Once the background worker has processed an item, its `digio_response` field holds Digio's raw response verbatim (extracted from the stored evidences); a still-PENDING item, or one whose failure never reached Digio (e.g. a transport error), instead has `verification_errors` populated and no `digio_response`. 404 if the request_id doesn't exist, 400 if it's missing or not a valid UUID. Note: this GET endpoint has no precedent in the design doc — it's an addition needed to satisfy 'return Digio's response' for this inherently asynchronous flow.
